paragraphs: On Saturday morning, the Explorers went to the small zoo. The bus stopped at the zoo gate at nine o'clock. Teacher Kim gave each child a map. "Alright, listen," she said. "We have two hours, and we will visit three areas." "First we will see the birds, then the tigers, and last the monkeys." Lily had her notebook, and she wanted to copy the facts from the signs. Mia had her camera, Leo had his pencil, and May had a list of questions.

The bird area was big and green. Many small birds sat in the trees, and their singing was beautiful. One bird was yellow, and another bird had a long blue tail. "How many birds can you see?" asked Mia. Leo counted slowly. "Six," he said, "but one is hiding behind a leaf." Mia took three photos of the yellow bird.

Next, they walked to the tiger area. A big tiger lay under a tree, and it did not move. It had black stripes on its orange body. One stripe on its back was as wide as a hand. There was a screen next to the glass, and it showed facts about tigers. "Every tiger has different stripes," Lily read. "A tiger sleeps for sixteen hours a day," she read next. Lily copied both facts in her notebook. "That tiger is lazy," said Leo. "I know a boy who sleeps like that." Mia laughed.

After that, they went to the monkey area. A zookeeper in a green shirt was giving fruit to the monkeys. "May, now you can ask your questions," said Teacher Kim. May felt a little nervous, but she smiled and asked, "What do the monkeys eat?" "They eat bananas, mangoes, and some leaves," said the zookeeper. "How often do you feed them?" asked May. "Three times a day," he answered. A small monkey sat on its mother's back, and Mia took a photo of them.

At eleven o'clock, the bus was waiting at the gate. The children sat on the bus and looked at their notes. Lily had two facts, and Mia had twenty photos. Leo had one cartoon of a lazy tiger, and May had two answers. "Alright, that is enough for a good blog post," said Teacher Kim. Lily smiled and said, "I will write it tonight."
